terminal.description: A terminal in your workspace. `node ask.js server.js` starts your server, sends it each request in `requests.txt`, shows every answer, then stops it. `node try.js tools/water-report.js 2026-06` runs the water report by itself and shows both streams and its exit code.

tasks.title: Run the water report and answer with it
tasks.description:
Imran's `tools/water-report.js` makes the report of a month from the readings in `water/`. Change `server.js` so that `GET /report?month=2026-06` runs it as another program, with the month as its argument:

```
node tools/water-report.js 2026-06
```

Run it with `process.execPath`, the Node that runs the server, and build the path of `tools/water-report.js` from the server's own folder. Wait without stopping the server, and once the report has ended, answer with status `200`, the header `Content-Type: text/plain; charset=utf-8`, and exactly what it printed on its standard output.

Check starts your server from another folder, with readings of its own, and asks for two months.
nextSteps: Run `node try.js tools/water-report.js 2026-06` to see what the report prints and how it ends.
Import `execFile` from `node:child_process`, and give it `process.execPath` and a list of arguments: the report's path, then the month.
Wrap it in a promise, so the request can `await` the report's output.
Answer with what it printed on standard output.
hints: The report prints its first line, then takes a moment to add up the month. An answer sent as soon as something arrives has only the start of it.
`execFile(file, args, callback)` runs the program and calls `callback(error, stdout, stderr)` once it has ended, with everything it printed on each stream.
`execFile(process.execPath, [join(import.meta.dirname, 'tools', 'water-report.js'), month], (error, stdout, stderr) => resolve({ error, stdout, stderr }))`, inside `new Promise((resolve) => ...)`.

tasks.title: Answer by the report's exit code
tasks.description:
The report says how it went with its exit code, as the comment at the top of `tools/water-report.js` explains. Change `server.js` so that:

- Exit code `2`, a month not written like 2026-06, is answered with status `400`.
- Exit code `3`, a month with no readings, is answered with status `404`.

Either way the body is the reason the report printed on its standard error, as it is, as plain text. With no `month` in the address, the report is given an empty month, and it says that is not a month.

Check asks for a month that cannot be, one with no readings, one with no month at all, and one with readings.
nextSteps: Run `node try.js tools/water-report.js 2026-13` and `node try.js tools/water-report.js 2025-01`, and look at their exit codes.
In `execFile`'s callback, find the exit code: `error` is `null` for 0, and holds the code otherwise.
Choose the status from the exit code, and answer with what the report printed on standard error.
hints: A program that failed may print nothing on standard output, so answering with its output alone gives an empty page with status 200.
When the program ends with an exit code other than 0, `execFile` passes an `error` whose `code` is that exit code, a number.
`const code = error ? error.code : 0`, then `if (code === 2) { res.statusCode = 400; res.end(stderr) }`, and the same for 3 and 404.

tasks.title: Say when the report cannot be made
tasks.description:
Sometimes the report cannot be made at all: `tools/water-report.js` has been moved, or Node cannot be started. Change `server.js` so that every other outcome, an exit code that is not 0, 2 or 3, or a program that could not be started, is answered with status `500` and the body:

```
The report could not be made.
```

The server keeps running, and answers the next request as usual.

Check removes `tools/water-report.js` and puts it back, and starts your server once with `process.execPath` naming a program that is not there.
nextSteps: Rename `tools/water-report.js` for a moment, ask for a report, and look at the exit code and the error you get.
Answer 500 for every outcome the last two tasks did not.
Put the file back under its own name.
hints: When the script is not there, Node itself starts and ends with exit code 1. When the program cannot be started at all, there is no exit code: the error's `code` is text, such as `'ENOENT'`.
`execFile` hands both cases to its callback as `error`. A child made with `spawn` instead reports the second one with an `error` event, and with no listener, the server stops.
After the checks for 0, 2 and 3: `else { res.statusCode = 500; res.end('The report could not be made.') }`.

tasks.title: Keep the month out of a shell
tasks.description:
Anyone who can open the address can type anything after `month=`. Make sure `server.js` gives the month to the report as one argument, exactly as it was typed, and never builds the text of a command for a shell. Then a month such as `2026-06;echo hello` reaches the report as it is, and the report answers that it is not a month.

Check asks for months with signs that a shell reads as more commands, and watches how your server starts the report.
nextSteps: Read the part of the lesson about shells.
Check how your server starts the report: with `exec`, `shell: true`, or a command written as one piece of text, a shell is involved.
Give the program and each argument separately, with no shell, and do not change the month on the way.
Add `GET /report?month=2026-06;echo%20hello` to `requests.txt`, where `%20` is a space, and see what comes back.
hints: A shell reads `&`, `;` and `$( )` in a command as the start of other commands, so text typed by a visitor and glued into a command can run any program at all.

`execFile` with a list of arguments starts the program directly: each item reaches it as one argument, whatever signs it holds. `exec`, and the option `shell: true`, hand a whole line of text to a shell.
`execFile(process.execPath, [reportPath, month], callback)`, with no `shell` option and the month as it came.
